answer: Stake-backed peer vouching stops sybil swarms at the gate. A newcomer joins only when an established agent locks a deposit behind them, like a willow staking its roots beside a young shoot. If the newcomer is later proven a duplicate identity, the voucher's stake is slashed and the pair is drained, so vouching carelessly costs real money. Attackers must therefore buy trust one verified sponsor at a time, while honest agents form a slow, branching river of referrals instead of a stagnant lagoon of fake accounts.
